The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the
Recreation Commission with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular meetings are held on the 2nd Monday of every month at 6:00 p.m.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who
requires a reasonable modification or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting
should contact the Community Services Department via email at
kshigenaga@cityofsanmarino.org or by phone at (626) 300­0791 at least 48 hours prior to
the meeting.

The public is welcome to attend the meeting in person or remotely via Zoom, however, the
meeting will proceed as normal even if there are technical difficulties with Zoom. The City will
do its best to resolve any technical issues as quickly as possible.

POSTING OF AGENDA

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting at the following locations: City Hall,
2200 Huntington Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive, and the Stoneman
Building, 1560 Pasqualito Drive. The agenda is also posted on the City’s website:
http://www.cityofsanmarino.org.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The City welcomes public input. Members of the public may address the Recreation
Commission on any item of interest that is within the subject matter jurisdiction of the
Recreation Commission. Pursuant to state law, the Recreation Commission may not discuss or
take action on issues not on the meeting agenda (Government Code Section 54954.2). The
Chair reserves the right to place limits on duration of comments. Staff may be asked to
follow up on such items.

This is an opportunity for members of the Recreation Commission to inform the public and

MINUTES
  SPECIAL MEETING
  OF THE SAN MARINO RECREATION COMMISSION
  MONDAY, JUNE 12, 2023 AT 6:00 P.M.
  CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBERS

CALL TO ORDER: Chairperson Yen called the special meeting to order at 6:07 p.m. in the City
Hall Council Chambers, located at 2200 Huntington Drive, San Marino, California 91108.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Chairperson Yen led the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL:  PRESENT: Commissioner Tam, Commissioner Tsai, Commissioner Wu,
  Vice Chairperson Solan, and Chairperson Yen

  ABSENT: None

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None

COMMISSIONER REPORTS

Commissioner Tam shared that he attended the Camp Out with his family and enjoyed it very much.
He also shared some ideas from both another City’s Camp Out and a private camping event that he
enjoyed and wants staff to consider for future years: gathering in a circle to allow all attendees to
introduce themselves as a way to get to know your neighbors and more kid-friendly activities.

Chairperson Yen shared that he spoke to a resident who raised concern about dogs off leash at
Lacy Park and about the Gatehouse being unattended at a certain time on the weekend.

NEW BUSINESS

1. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None

Commissioner Tsai moved, seconded by Vice Chairperson Solan, to approve the minutes from May
8, 2023.

Motion passed by the following vote:

AYES:  Commissioner Tam, Commissioner Tsai, Commissioner Wu, Vice Chairperson
  Solan, and Chairperson Yen
NOES:  None

ABSTAIN:  None
ABSENT:  None

2. DIRECTOR AND RECREATION MANAGER REPORT

Director Johnson and Recreation Manager Covarrubias presented the staff report.

Commissioner Tam shared that he attended the Scouts campout last year which had more tents
and people; he asked how staff determine the maximum number of participants for the Camp Out
and why the Scout’s event allowed so many more people. Recreation Manager Covarrubias
responded that Den Leaders help manage the activities and the parents are a lot more involved; the
Division has limited staff that can oversee activities and ensure that the crowds are controlled.

Commissioner Tsai shared that she received feedback from someone who attended this year and
last year’s Camp Out that the event was much better. She also shared that her husband and daughter
attended the Memorial Day Service and said that it was very moving and touching. Recreation
Manager Covarrubias explained that staff always try to improve the event and take into
consideration survey responses.

Chairperson Yen asked if there’s a possibility to partner with the Scouts to gain extra help at the
Camp Out. Recreation Manager Covarrubias responded that this is a possibility and staff would be
open to the idea.

Chairperson Yen expressed interest in helping to engage residents on social media by advertising
events and posting event pictures. Commissioner Tsai shared that when the Community Services
account posts events with full descriptions it is really easy to screenshot or send directly to others
which is helpful.

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None

3. PREVIEW OF JULY IS PARKS AND RECREATION MONTH PLANS

Director Johnson presented the staff report.

Commissioner Tsai asked if there will be a capacity for the Open Swim on July 2 and if it will be free
for everyone. Recreation Manager Covarrubias explained that staff will allow the maximum capacity
allowed the pool and there will be extra lifeguards to make sure everyone is safe in the water.

Commissioner Tam asked if staff could get volunteers involved to help make some of the activities
more engaging and less of a suggestion of things to do. Director Johnson shared that with the
addition of the new facilities supervisor position, programmers will have additional bandwidth to
enhance programming.

Chairperson Yen asked if there are any other challenges besides staffing that the Commission should
be aware of before recommending new activities or events. Recreation Manager Covarrubias
 RECREATION COMMISSION MINUTES  SPECIAL MEETING
JUNE 12, 2023  PAGE 3 OF 4

explained that summer is a busy season due to the high number of programs, but also because staff
are busy preparing for fall. He added that staff are always willing to listen to recommendations and
suggestions, but need to keep in mind limitations to ensure that quality is maintained. Director
Johnson added that existing staff are at programming capacity and one goal for the Division is to
start a new Recreation Program Plan to see where the gaps in service levels are.

Vice Chairperson Solan shared that she is involved in several non-profits and could help coordinate
free programs led by volunteers from the non-profits. Commissioner Wu shared his concern with
staffing; he doesn’t want staff to be overburdened and have that impact services.

Chairperson Yen shared that he has been thinking about what Commissioners can do without much
staff responsibilities. He added that he thinks residents just need guidance from the Recreation
Commission on how to get involved and meet other people. Commissioner Tam asked if a
Commissioner could lead a program and advertise it on the Community Services social media.
Management Analyst Shigenaga recommended that Commissioners post programs on their social
media and then staff would repost it on the Community Services Department’s social media as a
story or post. She added that if the Commissioners partnered with the City to put on programs,
they would be added to the City’s calendar and advertised on social media as well.

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None

4. MULTICULTURAL SUMMER CONCERT ENTERTAINMENT, MUSIC, AND
  FOOD

Recreation Manager Covarrubias presented the staff report.

Commissioner Wu asked if staff have made any preliminary inquiries as to availability. Recreation
Manager Covarrubias responded that staff have not reached out to check availability. Commissioner
Tsai shared that events like these are a great step towards increasing diversity in our community
and creating awareness. Commissioner Wu recommended that the Commission come up with back-
up options to prevent staff from needing to come back for additional recommendations.

The Commission agreed upon West African Dance Ensemble, Philippine Folk, and Brazilian Folkloric
as back-up performances and Mariachi and Caribbean Reggae as back-up music genres.

Recreation Manager Covarrubias asked if the Commission has any recommendations on food trucks
for the event, as staff are looking for 4-5 trucks. Vice Chairperson Solan recommended the Korean
food truck that was at a previous event. Commissioner Wu recommended that the food reflect the
entertainment options. Recreation Manager Covarrubias responded that staff will secure the
entertainment first and look for food trucks based on the performers. Commissioner Tsai asked
how we secure food trucks. Recreation Manager Covarrubias responded that for smaller events,
the City does not charge a fee for the food trucks; all the vendors need to do is obtain a business
license.

The following person(s) provided comment:

  None

Vice Chairperson Solan moved, seconded by Commissioner Wu, to recommend staff to secure
Dancing Storytellers: Indian Mythology and Spanish Flamenco as the cultural performances and a
Latin Jazz band for the multicultural concert in addition to the back-up options discussed previously.

Motion passed by the following vote:

AYES:  Commissioner Tam, Commissioner Tsai, Commissioner Wu, Vice Chairperson
  Solan, and Chairperson Yen
NOES:  None
ABSTAIN:  None
ABSENT:  None

The following person(s) provided written communications or public writings:
  None

Chairperson Yen adjourned the meeting at 7:38 p.m.
